name: TN-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+11 district with a longtime incumbent running for re-election
Prediction markets price DesJarlais at roughly 97% to win
Fundraising blowout: DesJarlais has $523K on hand versus Broderick's $8.6K
No polls or expert ratings show competition, and two independents further fragment opposition
model.rationale: Every available signal points to a comfortable Republican hold: the district's strong Republican lean, DesJarlais's incumbency and overwhelming cash advantage, and markets pricing his win odds near 97% leave the underfunded Democratic challenger little visible path.
model.watch: A late influx of outside Democratic spending or a scandal-driven collapse in DesJarlais's support would be the main forces that could move this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South-central Tennessee's fourth district leans firmly Republican, and incumbent Scott DesJarlais is seeking re-election with the advantages that status brings. He has raised about $635,000 and holds more than $500,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Victoria Broderick has raised under $85,000 with less than $10,000 available late in the cycle. Two independent candidates also appear on the ballot, further dividing any opposition vote.

No public polls or expert ratings track the race, but prediction markets give DesJarlais roughly a 97% chance of winning, and the district's fundamentals point the same way. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of polling, which keeps uncertainty elevated in absolute terms even as the direction of the race is clear. Barring an unexpected shift, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin in November.
